name: room
description: Rooms and interior spaces for buildings or dungeons

entries.value: Bedroom — bed, chest, washstand, personal keepsakes, and evidence of the occupant's last activity.
Living Room — worn seating around a hearth with family objects and a concealed letter.
Kitchen — preparation tables, ovens, knives, stored food, and something recently left cooking.
Dining Hall — long tables, serving doors, faded decoration, and seating arranged by status.
Toilet — basic sanitation, a narrow vent, cleaning supplies, and graffiti from previous users.
Pantry — shelves of preserved food with one wall sounding hollow when struck.
Storeroom — labeled crates, spare furniture, dust, and one item that clearly does not belong.
Office — desk, correspondence, account books, locked drawers, and an appointment calendar.
Workshop — specialized tools, unfinished work, material scraps, and a dangerous active device.
Guardroom — weapon racks, duty roster, cards, half-eaten meals, and an alarm mechanism.
Cell — restraints, scratched messages, stale water, and signs of an impossible escape.
Library — packed shelves, reading desks, ladders, catalogues, and a deliberately misfiled book.
Laboratory — stained benches, fragile instruments, sealed samples, and an experiment still progressing.
Armory — maintained weapons, armor stands, issue records, and several conspicuous empty spaces.
Infirmary — narrow beds, medical tools, medicine cabinets, and patient notes written in code.
Chapel — benches, sacred images, offerings, and a small private confessional passage.
Bathing Room — heated pool, drains, towels, privacy screens, and access to maintenance tunnels.
Nursery — small beds, toys, lesson boards, and protective symbols painted beneath the furniture.
Ballroom — polished floor, musicians' gallery, chandeliers, and balconies designed for observation.
Map Room — wall maps, surveying tools, campaign markers, and one region intentionally erased.
Treasury — counted valuables, sealed chests, ownership records, and multiple layers of security.
Secret Passage — a cramped route with spy holes, old footprints, and a mechanism opening elsewhere.
Ritual Chamber — geometric markings, restraints, consumed offerings, and lingering supernatural pressure.
Portal Room — a reinforced chamber centered on an inactive gate and emergency shutdown controls.
Trophy Gallery — preserved beasts, captured banners, named weapons, and a display that is still alive.
Interrogation Room — fixed chair, soundproof walls, drainage channel, and carefully organized questions.
